title: Posting Money to a Ridgecrest Advantage Premium Account
content:
Money the member pays on a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan is posted against the oldest unpaid coverage month first, and the balance effect recorded on the entry says whether it left part of the balance outstanding, settled it exactly, or exceeded it.

### Conditions of record

- The enrollment is in a status of coverage in force, coverage in its premium grace period, or coverage terminated for non-payment on the day the money is posted. The enrollment record is the authority, tested before the money is posted and matched on the enrollment reference.
- No payment entry carrying the same remittance reference and the same amount is already posted on this enrollment. The premium account of that enrollment is the authority, tested before the money is posted; two payment entries are told apart by the date they were posted and the coverage month they belong to.

### Overpayment

An overpayment is refunded by the channel the money arrived on — the channel recorded on the payment entry — and is never held against a coverage month the plan has not yet billed.

### Credit adjustments

A credit adjustment always names the single premium charge it relieves and the reason it was granted. The remaining words of this clause, that a credit adjustment *may never exceed the amount of that charge; a credit larger than one charge is split across the charges it relieves*, are no longer in force and are not applied to a credit adjustment posted on a Ridgecrest Advantage premium account.

### Money arriving after termination

Money that arrives after termination is accepted only while the reinstatement window is still open and is refunded in full where reinstatement is not granted; it never by itself restores coverage.

### What the member says, and what the record shows

A member's statement that they have paid is a reason to look for the money, never a reason to post it: nothing is credited until the payment is on the plan's record.

*A member says a cheque cleared last week and nothing appears on the premium account.* The statement is a reason to look for the money. Until the payment stands on the plan's record, nothing is credited.
